business: Quilt: a personal app builder. Describe the app you need and an AI assistant builds it; the assistant fills any app from a photo, sentence, file or connector; syncs phone and laptop
why_not: My notes live in Apple Notes and Google Docs, they already sync between my phone and laptop, and I can already snap a whiteboard into a note. I might poke at the free tier once, but I'm not paying $6 a month to rebuild a setup that already works.

My notes live in Goodnotes on my iPad and I like writing by hand, and whatever else I track is already in Notion for free. I might poke at the free tier once out of curiosity, but I'm not paying another $6 a month to move my stuff somewhere new.

Honestly, the mess of five apps is my actual problem, so I'd download the free version and poke at it. But I make about seven grand a year and I'm already paying for Spotify and a budgeting app, so another $6 a month isn't happening unless Quilt replaces something I already pay for.
I don't pay for apps, period. If it's actually good I'd poke at the free tier, but 5 apps is probably enough for me, and my Notes app and Google Docs already do most of this for nothing.

It's brand new, so there are no Play ratings or Reddit threads for me to read, and I don't pay for apps nobody has reviewed. I might try the free tier, but 5 apps is enough for my lists and I make $14k a year, so I'm not paying $6 a month for this.

It's brand new, so there are no Play Store ratings or Reddit threads for me to check, and I don't pay for apps I can't look up first. At most I'd poke at the free tier, and I already know I'd drop it after a week like every other tracker I've set up.
flip: A one-tap import of my existing Notes and Google Docs that sorts them into folders for me, plus an easy full export so I'm never locked in.
If I could snap a page of my handwritten Goodnotes notes and it reliably turned them into something searchable and sorted, and that kept working for a month on the free tier.

If it imported my whole Obsidian vault or Notion workspace and the whiteboard-to-organized-notes thing was so good I kept reaching for it after the first week, without me having to rebuild everything.
If after a few weeks on the free tier it actually let me cancel my budgeting app, so Plus costs me nothing extra, or if there was a student price around $2 to $3 a month.
A free student or first-year deal, plus whiteboard photos turning into clean, searchable notes far better than just saving the picture in Google Docs.
A few months of solid reviews and Reddit posts from students saying the AI got their apps right the first time, and that they hit the free limit and found Plus worth it.
A clear promise that my data is private and not used for training, plus one-tap export to plain files or Google Docs, so trying it costs me nothing if I leave.
A free student plan through my university, or the free tier being generous enough that I never hit the wall.
If it actually replaced my budgeting app so I could cancel that subscription, and I was still opening it every day after a month on the free plan.
If I was still opening it every day after a month because the purchase-to-budget thing actually replaced my budgeting app, so I could cancel that and pay for this instead.
If it imported my Notion databases cleanly and the snap-a-receipt or whiteboard-to-the-right-database part saved me real time every week, something Notion still makes me do by hand.
If it could pull in my whole Goodnotes library in one go and let me keep writing with the pencil on my iPad, so I'm not running two note apps.
A few months of solid 4.5+ ratings and Reddit posts from people my age saying they still use it daily, plus the free tier actually being enough to prove it sticks for me.
If it could pull in my existing notes and workout history from the apps I already use, for free, in a few minutes, so switching costs me nothing.
If it could pull in my existing Notes and Google Docs in one tap and export everything back out just as easily, and the snap-a-whiteboard thing actually saved me real time every week.

A one-tap Notion import plus a full export to Markdown/CSV, and a plain statement that my data isn't used to train anything. Then the snap-a-receipt and talk-to-log stuff might be worth $6 because Notion is clunky on my phone.
A one-tap import that pulls in my existing notes, budget and workout history and actually gets it right, so I'm not starting from zero.
A clear privacy policy plus one-click full export (CSV or Markdown) and a Notion import that keeps my databases, so switching costs me nothing.
If it could import all my Apple Notes and Google Docs in one tap and export them back out just as easily, and the free tier was enough that I'd only pay once I was already hooked.
A student deal where Plus is free or like $1-2 a month with a school email, or the free tier giving enough actions to cover a whole semester of lecture photos.
